title: A circuit dissection of perception–action decoupling in S-ketamine-induced hallucination-like states
title_zh: S‑氯胺酮诱导的幻觉状态中感知–行动解耦的电路解剖
abstract: Hallucinations are a core feature of several psychiatric disorders, but the circuit mechanisms that separate perception from behavioral output remain poorly defined. Here, we combined an auditory discrimination task with AI-based pose analysis to quantify S-ketamine-induced false auditory threat responses and behavioral disorganization in mice. Control assays, including sucrose preference, loss of righting reflex, and prepulse inhibition, indicated that these effects were not explained by anhedonia, anesthesia, or basic auditory deficits. Using in vivo fiber photometry, single-cell miniscope calcium imaging, and pathway-specific chemogenetic and optogenetic manipulations, we identified dissociable circuit contributions within convergent striatal pathways. The basolateral amygdala to caudal striatum pathway (BLA→TS) supported salience-weighted perceptual decisions and, when aberrantly recruited by S-ketamine, promoted auditory false alarms. In contrast, the medial prefrontal cortex to caudal striatum pathway (mPFC→TS) primarily shaped behavioral expression and, when dysregulated, generated disorganized action patterns. At the network level, S-ketamine shifted TS activity from a sparse, high-contrast state to a high-frequency, low-amplitude, diffusely coupled state, consistent with reduced integrative precision. Auditory cortex to TS inputs were not broadly suppressed, supporting pathway specificity. Bidirectional chemogenetic manipulation of BLA→TS and mPFC→TS pathways in drug-naive mice further supported the TS as an integrative node linking perceptual evaluation to behavioral output. Dexmedetomidine co-administration restored pathway-level temporal dynamics and reorganized TS network coupling without simply suppressing activity. Together, these findings define a circuit framework for NMDAR-antagonist-induced hallucination-like states and provide a mechanistic rationale for dexmedetomidine-mediated mitigation of S-ketamine-associated perceptual and behavioral disruption.
abstract_zh: 幻觉是多种精神疾病的核心特征，但将感知与行为输出分离的电路机制尚未明晰。我们将听觉辨别任务与基于人工智能的姿态分析相结合，量化了S‑氯胺酮诱导的小鼠听觉假威胁反应和行为紊乱。包括甜味偏好、翻身反射丧失和预脉冲抑制在内的对照实验表明，这些效应并非由无快感、麻醉或基本听觉缺陷所致。通过体内光纤光谱学、单细胞微型摄像头钙成像以及通路特异性的化学遗传学和光遗传学操控，我们识别了汇聚纹状体通路中可分离的电路贡献。基底外侧杏仁核至尾纹状体通路（BLA→TS）支持以显著性加权的感知决策，并在S‑氯胺酮异常招募时促进听觉误报；相反，内侧前额叶皮层至尾纹状体通路（mPFC→TS）主要塑造行为表达，失调时产生无序的行动模式。在网络层面，S‑氯胺酮将TS活动从稀疏、高对比状态转变为高频、低幅、弥散耦合状态，符合整合精度降低。听觉皮层至TS的输入并未被广泛抑制，支持通路特异性。对药物前小鼠进行BLA→TS和mPFC→TS通路的双向化学遗传学操控进一步支持TS作为将感知评估与行为输出连接的整合节点。地塞米松与S‑氯胺酮共同给药恢复了通路层面的时间动力学，并在不单纯抑制活动的情况下重组了TS网络耦合。综上，这些发现为NMDAR拮抗剂诱导的幻觉状态提供了电路框架，并为地塞米松缓解S‑氯胺酮相关感知与行为紊乱提供了机制性依据。
